blocked_what: e1's four 60-iter ms/token reps on card 5, ten minutes, and its 10-minute QUEUE_TIMEOUT would have reported the holder as still running
cause: a setsid backgrounded child whose wrapper exits immediately leaves nobody to wait() it, so an unreapable zombie is the GUARANTEED end state of the pod's launch shape, not an anomaly (b0's correction: there was no wait in the wrapper) -- and every liveness reader in card_claim.py says a zombie is alive, measured: os.kill(3891063,0) ALIVE, /proc entry present, ps -o stat= Zs, so claims() filed the corpse as a live claim and acquire kept refusing the card
fix_applied: card_claim.py status now names ZOMBIE as a third claim/card disagreement with the pid state and claim age, exits nonzero, and does not auto-break: a human releases (6e ruling, reviewer e1)

blocked_what: git merge, before any merge driver runs
cause: a dirty runs/friction.jsonl or data/pod_head_manifest.txt aborts the merge with 'local changes would be overwritten' at the pre-merge tree check, which happens BEFORE merge drivers are consulted, so a driver for a derived file cannot help while that file sits dirty
fix_applied: git checkout HEAD -- <both>, merge, re-append (stash is banned repo-wide). Root fix candidate: harness friction add commits its own row path-scoped in the same call

blocked_what: python3 scripts/card_claim.py --selftest run by hand from a shell -- the first four cases red at 8393d579, before today's edits
cause: the selftest's in-process acquire() calls passed no pid, so the holder defaulted to os.getppid() = whatever invoked the selftest: python from a wrapper (22/22 green) and the SHELL from a terminal, where acquire correctly refuses to bind a shell. A selftest whose answer depends on its caller is testing the caller
fix_applied: pid=os.getpid() on every in-process acquire; this process is python by construction. The shell-refusal behaviour keeps its own dedicated world built with a real shell. 28/28 from both parents
